questions.stem: A reaction profile shows reactants at 80 kJ, a peak at 200 kJ, and products at 50 kJ. What is the activation energy for the forward reaction?
questions.explanation: The activation energy for the forward reaction is the difference between the peak (transition state) and the reactants: Ea = 200 - 80 = 120 kJ. It is measured from the reactant energy level up to the highest point on the profile.

questions.stem: When a catalysed reaction profile is drawn alongside an uncatalysed one, which features stay the same?

options.text: The activation energy and the transition state
The energy of the reactants and products, and the value of ΔH
Only the energy of the reactants stays the same
Everything changes when a catalyst is added

questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with a lower peak, but it does not change the energy of the reactants or products. Therefore, ΔH remains the same. Only the activation energy (height of the peak) is reduced.
